all.name: Sets and counting principles
all.description: Set notation, Venn diagrams, inclusion-exclusion and the rule of product.
objectives: use set notation for union, intersection and complement
visualize set operations with Venn diagrams
apply inclusion-exclusion to count elements
apply the rule of product to count outcomes

all.name: Permutations and combinations
all.description: Counting ordered and unordered selections and using them to compute probabilities.
objectives: count permutations of a set
compute combinations with binomial coefficients
compute probabilities by counting equally likely outcomes

all.name: Conditional probability and total probability
all.description: Defining conditional probability and using the multiplication rule, law of total probability and trees.
objectives: compute conditional probability from the definition
use the multiplication rule
apply the law of total probability over a partition
organize computations with probability trees

all.name: Independence of events
all.description: Defining and checking independence of events and its paradoxes.
objectives: state the definition of independent events
check whether two events are independent
explain why a probability-zero event is independent of itself

all.name: Bayes' theorem and base rate fallacy
all.description: Inverting conditional probabilities with Bayes' theorem, illustrated by screening tests.
objectives: compute an inverted conditional probability with Bayes' theorem
explain the base rate fallacy
analyze screening test false positives

all.name: Random variables, pmf and cdf
all.description: Random variables as payoff functions and their probability mass and cumulative distribution functions.
objectives: define a discrete random variable on a sample space
write the pmf of a random variable
compute and graph a cdf
state properties of the cdf

all.name: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric distributions
all.description: Named discrete distributions, their models and pmfs, and arithmetic with random variables.
objectives: identify Bernoulli, binomial, geometric and uniform models
derive the binomial pmf by counting
compute geometric probabilities
add random variables and count successes with indicators

all.name: Bayes tables: prior, likelihood, posterior
all.description: Terminology and tabular form of Bayes' theorem for updating discrete priors.
objectives: identify hypotheses, data, prior, likelihood and posterior
build a Bayesian update table
compute prior and posterior pmfs
distinguish probability of data from probability of hypotheses

all.name: Repeated updating and screening
all.description: Updating posteriors with successive data and revisiting the base rate fallacy.
objectives: use a posterior as the next prior
update on multiple data points at once
solve a screening test example with a Bayes table
